one_line_contribution: A controlled ALFWorld manipulation of how widely a planted object-receptacle binding holds (one receptacle per class everywhere / per (scene,class) / per game) that reads off, at each scope, the smallest static cached prompt that matches top-k retrieval, and how much of the retrieval gain at instance scope is nothing but the eval game's own duplicate trajectory.
closest_prior_work: No single verified paper makes this claim. The two closest, both verified via the literature command (s2cli.py paper): (1) EvoMemBench, arXiv:2605.18421 (verified, S2: 'two axes: memory scope (in-episode vs. cross-episode) and memory content'; long-context baselines outperform specialized memory methods). It does not threaten the binding-scope manipulation — its 'scope' is temporal, not the scope over which a binding holds — but its headline that long context beats memory methods pre-empts a good part of the whole-bank message the proposal builds arms for (P7's interest is then 'why does the whole bank lose here', not 'does it lose'). (2) The Compliance Trap, arXiv:2607.10608 (verified, S2: Enter-Propagation-Recovery, agents adopt conflicting retrieved memory early and compound errors). It is cited, but it substantially pre-empts P6(b): if agents already fail to discount contradicted memory, 'conflict ≈ neutral' is the expected direction, and the proposal frames it as a discovery rather than a replication under a cleaner manipulation. One item my search turned up that the proposal does NOT cite and should: ExecRetrieval, arXiv:2609.01865 (hf, 2026-09-01), which plants controlled, execution-verified single-edit near-clone variants of each query's canonical item in the retrieval pool — the same planted-near-duplicate design move, in code retrieval, judged on embedding discrimination rather than on downstream gain share. Also adjacent and uncited: 'Right Family, Wrong Skill', arXiv:2606.10388 (hf), on same-family sibling exposure in skill retrieval, which is close to the conflict-neighbour arm.
strongest_objection: Most rungs of the ladder are true by construction, so the ladder measures Qwen3-32B's reading competence rather than a property of memory. The relocation rules define the information content of the bank: at global scope the 20-sentence compiled prefix is an information-complete restatement of the planted rule, at scene scope the (scene,class) table is likewise complete, and at instance scope 'no static prefix smaller than one row per instance exists' is a definition the proposal states outright ('the instance-scope static substitute is defined as a prefix whose size does not grow with the number of instances; the O(instances) duplicate-row table ... is not run'). P2 and P4 can therefore only be falsified by a format/lookup failure, and the headline P6(a) is worse: the automated entailment check calls it near-entailed and it is — instance-scope relocation is built so another game's duplicate carries zero information about this game's placement, and the added foreign duplicates can only displace same-scene train items at ranks 1-3, pushing N(0.5) down, i.e. toward confirmation. The design contains no positive control showing that a strategy-transfer channel is detectable at all on this node, so P6(a) is a null the construction guarantees, reported as a finding. Strip the entailed rungs and what is left that could genuinely surprise is P0 (does the natural bank's +17.2 compile into a ~430-token class-location table?) and P6(b) — one confirmatory cell and one manipulated pair out of 22, for ~13.5k episodes. A secondary version of the same objection: P7's 'whole bank loses ≥14 net' is confounded by prefix length and item set, so a confirmation is readable as a many-shot dilution result (cf. arXiv:2510.16809, arXiv:2411.05000 in the brief), not as evidence that the query is doing work.
what_would_fix_it: Re-centre the paper on the cells that are not construction-determined and cut the ones that are. (1) Promote P0 to the headline: run the natural-bank scope estimate properly — class-location table, (scene,class) table, and a scrambled-binding version of each, paired with k3 and static3 on Measurement C's games and seeds — and report where the natural ALFWorld bank actually sits on the scope axis. That is a result about a benchmark the field uses, and it is not entailed. (2) Before claiming 'no spillover', run the bank-composition control the entailment check names: hold bank size, item count and rank composition fixed at instance scope and vary only whether the extra same-scene items are other games' exact duplicates or matched non-duplicate trajectories, plus a dose at s=0.25/0.75; show the strategy-transfer channel can be detected before reporting its absence. (3) Anchor P5's +28 to the measured absolute success of static3-relocated under the 25-step relocated regime and report the headroom; as written the threshold can fail for ceiling reasons rather than because the reader ignores its own duplicate. (4) Give P7 a length-matched control (80 same-scene items with the duplicate deleted, and 80 other-scene items) so a confirmation cannot be read as context dilution. (5) Either run the WebShop scope-statistic prediction or drop the framing that the scope of bindings is a general predictor — one environment, one reader, one synthetic relocation family cannot support it.
missing_baseline: A scrambled-binding placebo for every compiled static arm: the same sentence list / (scene,class) table with the class-to-receptacle mapping permuted, byte-identical in format and token count. Without it, 'the compiled sentence matches retrieval' cannot distinguish a reader that consumed the stated binding from a reader that ignored the prefix and found the object by search inside 25 steps — exactly the ambiguity blind1 was introduced to resolve for exemplars in Measurement C, and it is not carried over to the compiled arms. Two smaller omissions a reviewer would also ask for: a k=0 relocated arm per scope (the absolute anchor for how much room the bindings have, ~548 episodes each), and the instance-scope bank-composition control (matched non-duplicate same-scene items at fixed bank size) without which P6(a)'s null has no positive control.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My searches (all answered by the literature command, s2cli.py, with both channels reporting ok — s2=ok hf=ok on every call; WebSearch is unavailable in this session and was not used): (a) mechanism, --recent: 'binding scope near-duplicate leakage experience bank agent memory gain' -> 14 hits, closest arXiv:2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), arXiv:2605.11325 (Tenure, typed schemas with 'scope isolation' — storage scope, not binding scope), arXiv:2606.15903, arXiv:2512.16962; none manipulates duplicate rate or binding scope. (b) mechanism, all years: 'controlled duplicate rate in experience bank retrieval gain compiled static prompt agent' -> 16 hits, closest arXiv:2606.10388 (Right Family, Wrong Skill), arXiv:2608.11079 (SkillZip), arXiv:2602.08316 (SWE-ContextBench); no compiled-prompt-vs-retrieval arm at matched tokens with a manipulated duplicate rate. (c) closest named method: 'EvoMemBench memory scope in-episode cross-episode long-context baseline agent memory benchmark' --> arXiv:2605.18421 confirmed plus arXiv:2606.05684, arXiv:2605.12493, arXiv:2602.16313, arXiv:2606.13681; none compiles a bank into a static prefix or reports gain as a function of duplicate rate. (d) home literature: 'planted near-duplicate demonstration retrieval versus fixed exemplars in-context example selection inflation' -> only generic ICL selection work (arXiv:2405.00200, arXiv:2605.13511, arXiv:2309.07900), consistent with the proposal's claim that the contamination/dedup literature has not been applied to experience banks. (e) 'how much of agent memory benchmark gain comes from repeated near identical tasks leakage audit' --recent -> benchmark-validity work (arXiv:2605.12673 BenchJack, arXiv:2607.02577) but no leakage-share audit of memory gains. (f) 'ALFWorld object receptacle location instance specific binding memory retrieval scene' -> nothing on planted bindings. ID verification: I verified 2605.18421, 2606.02461, 2607.10608, 2511.20857, 2512.10696, 2602.08316, 2607.26497 and 2603.04814 with s2cli.py paper; all resolve and match the proposal's characterisations, including the important one that EvoMemBench's 'scope' is in-episode vs cross-episode and not binding scope. I did not verify 2604.07791, 2605.13880, 2603.21520, 2604.07487, 2605.24117 or the ConTAM/dedup IDs, which the proposal's argument leans on less directly. Judging the proposal's own check: it is better than most in this round — four query classes including a home-literature query without agent/memory vocabulary, both channels named, two IDs verified, and an honest statement of what each near-miss does and does not do. Its gap is recency at the very edge: it misses arXiv:2609.01865 (ExecRetrieval, 2026-09-01), which plants controlled near-clone variants of each query's canonical item in a retrieval pool, and arXiv:2606.10388; neither collides with the central claim, but both are the kind of preprint a reviewer will produce, and the second is a direct precedent for the conflict-neighbour construction. Novelty is scored on what I verified: the binding-scope manipulation against compiled static arms is unclaimed in the literature I could reach, so no cap applies.
